passage: Note from Trisha, Class 1 teacher at an after-school centre. At pick-up time, Deepika, six, was teased about her red lunch box by two classmates. She went to the corner of the reading sofa, pulled her knees to her chest and tucked her chin in. I sat a little way off and read my own book, near but not looking. After a while I said, "I'm here if you want." She didn't answer for a while, then leaned toward me and whispered, "They laughed."

qa.q: What did the classmates tease Deepika about?
qa.a: They teased her about her red lunch box.

qa.q: What might Deepika have been feeling when she pulled her knees to her chest and tucked her chin in?
qa.a: She was probably hurt and ashamed and wanted to hide. She might also have simply needed a quiet moment.

qa.q: Why did Trisha sit a little way off and read her own book?
qa.a: Trisha wanted to give Deepika a quiet presence without asking many questions, which let Deepika speak when she was ready.

qa.q: How might the classmates see Deepika's curling up?
qa.a: They might not realise how much the teasing hurt her, which is why an adult noticing matters.

grounding: A child curls up after being teased, and a quiet, non-intrusive presence works better than many questions.

passage: I am Baljeet, and at our after-school club I saw Lokesh, a classmate, sit on the beanbag with his shoulders hunched and his face turned into his knees. The teacher had told him off for running in the corridor, and he had been laughing before. Now he was very quiet and pulled his sleeves over his hands. Nobody spoke to him. After a while the club helper sat on the floor nearby with a picture book. I can't tell what Lokesh was feeling, maybe sad or ashamed.

qa.q: What had the teacher told Lokesh off for?
qa.a: The teacher had told him off for running in the corridor.

qa.q: What might Lokesh have been feeling as he hunched his shoulders and pulled his sleeves over his hands?
qa.a: He may have been sad or ashamed after being told off and wanted to hide. He might also have been tired after running about.

qa.q: What could the club helper do next if Lokesh stays curled up?
qa.a: The helper can stay nearby quietly, keep the picture book handy and let Lokesh come over when ready.

qa.q: How might Baljeet's view of Lokesh differ from the helper's?
qa.a: Baljeet only sees Lokesh being quiet and can't tell why, whereas the helper knows what happened earlier.

grounding: A child curls into himself after a scolding, and an observer can only guess at the feeling.

passage:
Monday: Ayesha came home from school, didn't take off her shoes, and curled up in the corner of the sofa, knees to chin. Sudha Nani didn't ask questions. She sat at the other end, knitting.
Tuesday: The same. Nani brought her warm milk and sat nearby, quietly.
Wednesday: Ayesha shuffled over and leaned on Nani. “They laughed at my plaits.” Nani stopped knitting. “That's not kind. Thank you for telling me.” That evening, Nani phoned the class teacher, who promised to speak to the children the next morning.

qa.q: What did Nani bring Ayesha on Tuesday?
qa.a: Warm milk.

qa.q: What does Ayesha curling up with her knees to her chin suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt sad and ashamed, and wanted to hide after being teased. Nani could not be sure at first what had happened.

qa.q: What did Nani do when Ayesha finally told her?
qa.a: She thanked her for telling, said the teasing was not kind, and phoned the class teacher that same evening.

qa.q: How might the class teacher see Nani's phone call?
qa.a: The teacher would likely be glad to know, so the children who laughed can be spoken to the next morning.

grounding: Over three days, a child curls up after being teased, and her grandmother's quiet presence helps her open up.

passage: The house was full of guests for Diwali, and Chandrika had three pans on the stove. She'd snapped at Siddharth for knocking over the rangoli colours. Now he was nowhere. She found him behind the curtain, hunched on the floor, chin tucked, arms wrapped round his knees. Guests were calling her. Chandrika sat down beside him anyway, saying nothing. After a minute, he leaned his head on her arm. “I'm sorry I shouted,” she said softly. He nodded, and she held him a moment longer.

qa.q: Where did Chandrika find Siddharth?
qa.a: Behind the curtain, hunched on the floor.

qa.q: What might Siddharth have been feeling when he hunched behind the curtain?
qa.a: He likely felt ashamed and sad after being snapped at for spilling the rangoli colours, and wanted to hide. He may also have felt overwhelmed by the busy house.

qa.q: What worked for Chandrika even with little time?
qa.a: She sat quietly beside him instead of asking many questions, and apologised gently once he leaned on her.

qa.q: What is it like for Chandrika to leave the guests and pans?
qa.a: It is hard, since everyone needs her, but she chose to give Siddharth her quiet presence first.

grounding: A child curls inward after being scolded during a busy festival, and his mother's quiet presence helps.

passage: Wasim came in from the colony park, went straight to the sofa and curled up, his face pressed into a cushion. His glasses lay on the floor. Jahnavi Phuppo put down her book. She didn't ask “What happened?” She just sat at the end of the sofa and gently rubbed his foot. After a while he mumbled into the cushion, “They called me four-eyes.” Phuppo said, “That was unkind, and it's not true about you.” She told his parents that evening, and they went to talk to the other boys' parents.

qa.q: What lay on the floor?
qa.a: Wasim's glasses.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling as he curled up with his face in the cushion?
qa.a: He was hurt and sad about being called names, and probably wanted to hide. He may also have felt embarrassed about his glasses.

qa.q: What made it easier for Wasim to speak?
qa.a: Phuppo stayed calm and close without questioning, so he felt safe enough to tell her.

qa.q: How might Wasim's parents feel when Phuppo tells them?
qa.a: They would likely feel upset for him and protective, which is why they went to talk to the other boys' parents.

grounding: A child curls inward after being teased, and his aunt's quiet presence helps him share it.

passage:
"Where's Sahil?"

"On the sofa. His cousin called him a crybaby at lunch."

Papa went in. "Sahil? What happened? Who said it? Why didn't you tell me? Are you hurt?"

Sahil pulled his knees up, tucked his chin and turned his face into the cushion.

"Let him be for a bit," Sangeeta said softly. She sat at the other end of the sofa with her tea and didn't say anything else.

After a while, Sahil's foot slid over to touch her leg.

"I'm here," she said.

"He laughed at me," he whispered.

qa.q: What did Sahil's cousin call him at lunch?
qa.a: A crybaby.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling when he tucked his chin and turned his face into the cushion?
qa.a: He was most likely hurt and ashamed after being teased, and wanted to hide. Papa's many questions may have made him feel even more crowded.

qa.q: Which approach worked better, and why?
qa.a: Sangeeta's quiet presence worked better than Papa's many questions, because it let Sahil come to her in his own time.

qa.q: How does Papa probably feel when Sahil curls up?
qa.a: Papa is likely worried and wants to fix things fast, which is why he asks so many questions at once.

grounding: It shows a child curling up after being teased and a quiet, non-intrusive presence working better than many questions.
